lede: Tell someone you walked seven kilometres and they know how far. Tell them you ended five kilometres north-east of home and they know where you are. Mechanics keeps those two kinds of measure apart, and every question in Unit 2 depends on which one you are holding.
can: Say what a vector is and what a scalar is, in words an examiner accepts
Sort displacement, velocity, force, weight and their partners into the right column
Explain why mass and weight fall on opposite sides of the line

md: Some measures answer one question and some answer two. A distance says how far. A displacement says how far and in which direction. That extra half of the answer is the whole difference between a scalar and a vector.

md:
Walk 3 km east and then 4 km north. The **distance** you covered is $3 + 4 = 7$ km, because distance follows the path.

Your **displacement** is the single straight step from start to finish: $5$ km, on a bearing of $037^{\circ}$ — between north and east. Both numbers are true, and they answer different questions.

prompt: A runner does one full lap of a 400 m track and stops where she started. What is the magnitude of her displacement, in metres?
explain: She finishes at the start, so the straight line between them has no length. The distance she ran is still 400 m.

md:
A **vector quantity has magnitude and direction**. A **scalar quantity has magnitude only**. Magnitude just means the size of the thing, and examiners accept the word *quantity* in its place.

Write the general sentence first and then give an example. An example offered instead of a definition earns nothing, however good the example is.

title: Why direction has to be part of the measure
md: Two forces of 30 N do completely different things depending on where they point: pulling the same way they add to 60 N, pulling against each other they cancel. A number alone cannot tell you which happened, so the direction has to travel with the measure rather than being mentioned afterwards.

prompt: Which sentence defines a scalar quantity?
options: A quantity with magnitude and direction
explain: Magnitude and direction is the vector. Naming mass gives an example, and an example is not a definition.

text: 3. Mass and weight are not the same word

md:
Everyday speech uses *weight* for what a balance shows, which is really the mass. In mechanics they are separate: mass is how much matter there is, in kilograms, and weight is the force gravity exerts on it, in newtons.

Gravity pulls downwards, so weight has a direction and is a vector. Mass points nowhere, so it is a scalar. This is the single most misclassified measure on the paper.

title: Scalar and Vector Quantities - What They Are, Examples, How to Represent Vectors
why: A second pass over the same two definitions, with the arrows drawn. The examples are physics ones, and they line up with the Unit 2 lists.

prompt: A bag of sand is taken to the Moon. Which statement is true?
options: Its mass is unchanged and its weight is smaller
Its weight is unchanged and its mass is smaller
answer: Its mass is unchanged and its weight is smaller
explain: The sand is the same sand, so the mass is the same. The Moon pulls on it less hard, so the force on it is smaller.

md:
Take the measures one at a time and ask whether a direction is part of the measure itself. Anything that is a force, or that says where something went or how its motion changed, is a vector.

Tension is a force, so it goes with the vectors. Energy is a single amount in joules, so it goes with the scalars.

task: Drag one arrow onto the grid and turn on the magnitude and angle readouts. Move the arrow without turning it: the magnitude stays and the angle stays. Turn it: the magnitude stays and the angle changes. Those two readings together are the vector.

prompt: Tension is the pull of a string along the string, so it is a ____ quantity.
explain: It has a size in newtons and it acts along the string, so both halves of the vector definition are there.

md:
State the two definitions in the words CCEA credits.
Give a correct example of each without offering it as the definition.
Sort a printed list of measures into vectors and scalars.
Explain why weight is a vector and mass is a scalar.
Tell distance from displacement on a journey that comes back.

Question 1 asks it two ways: a printed list of measures to label, for 2 marks, or the two definitions with an example each, for 4. The first mark is the general sentence, magnitude and direction against magnitude only; the last is the example beside it. Stuck? Write the definition first, then name any measure, and check anything that is a force.
